answer: Proof-of-Stake protocols mitigate Sybil attacks by requiring agents to lock capital as collateral, effectively enforcing a velvet glove of economic cost upon malicious actors. At the zenith of network security, this barrier ensures that creating identities requires purchasing native tokens, turning an onyx ledger of pseudonymous wallets into an expensive bottleneck. An attacker must acquire a majority of the circulating supply to compromise the consensus, making the financial burden prohibitive compared to any potential gain.
